text:
maria: Heads-up — running the nightly inference perf suite on ROCm nodes surfaced a regression vs NVIDIA. For long sequences (>=512, especially 1024) p95 latency jumps ~2–2.5x. We think it's a kernel availability gap causing a fallback path.

jonathan: Which kernel is missing?

maria: The fused attention kernel `attn_fused_v3` (the one we use for kv-friendly layout) isn't available / is unoptimized on our ROCm builds. Runtime falls back to `attn_ref` which does extra matmuls + memcpy. Quick snippet from the profiler: 

```
model: llama-13B-like
node: mi250 (rocm/5.6)
seq_len: 1024
p95 latency: 2.3x vs nvidia-A10
kernel used: attn_ref (fallback)
attn_ref breakdown:
  matmul(s): 42 ms
  kv memcpy: 18 ms
  layer overhead: 10 ms
  total attn: ~70 ms (per layer)
```

jonathan: Oof. That kv memcpy looks suspicious — do we know why it's happening on ROCm?

lee: It's the KV cache layout + ROCm buffer semantics. On NV we use an in-place interleaved KV layout that fused kernels read directly; on ROCm the folded layout isn't compatible so the fallback does explicit host-device/shuffle copies. Also ROCm lacks the optimized matmul path we select for short sequences -> so both kernel choice and copies hurt.

sam: Two-prong plan: 1) immediate mitigation: conditional routing in the router so requests hitting seq_len thresholds route off to nodes with working fused kernels (NVIDIA/dedicated pools) or to a compatible kernel-variant; 2) medium-term: autotune + per-node kernel inventory so router can make seq-length-aware picks automatically.

maria: Example of what I mean for a routing rule (sketch):

```
routing:
  conditional:
    - id: rocm-fallback-shortseq
      if: "gpu.arch == 'amd' and seq_len >= 512 and not kernel.available('attn_fused_v3')"
      route_to: "dedicated:nvidia-fused-pool"
    - id: rocm-attach-autotune
      if: "gpu.arch == 'amd' and kernel.available('attn_v2') and seq_len < 128"
      route_to: "local:fast-path"
```

jonathan: I like that. We should avoid brute-force routing that sends all traffic off-arch — use it for high-p95 tail requests only (canary first). Also we should surface this automatically in the Console per-model (kernel inventory + seq_len profile).

sam: For autotuning: suggest a per-node microbenchmark job that runs on startup / weekly and emits a small table: `kernel_id`, `seq_len`, `p50`, `p95`, `memory_safety` flags. Router reads that table and caches a TTL. If p95 for a kernel/seq combo > threshold then mark as degraded and prefer fallback routes.

alex: I'll try backporting the fused kernel to ROCm build — if we can get the kernel compiled then we can avoid routing. I'll open a PR for the ROCm kernel patches and run the microbench on an mi250. Assigning to me.

maria: Action items: @alex build/backport fused kernel; @maria add conditional routing policy + canary; @jonathan add console widgets for kernel inventory and seq_len histograms; @sam implement autotuner job. I'll add short-term threshold: route when p95_rocm / p95_ref > 1.5 AND seq_len >= 512.

ci-bot: perf-regression-check failed for nightly/inference/rocm-1024 — p95 increase 2.08x (baseline -> 2026-03-15T03:12Z). Link: https://ci.internal.redwood/perf/rocm-1024 (dashboard).

lee: One more detail — KV cache layout change will affect memory accounting in Dedicated pools (we may need to bump reservation on AMD nodes). Keep that in mind when routing to avoid OOMs.

jonathan: Agreed. Also add a fallback policy that picks a smaller model variant (e.g., 13B->7B) for long seq requests if routing capacity is exhausted.

maria: Great. I'll push a minimal router rule this afternoon with canary (5% traffic) and add logging so we can see cross-node latencies. :+1:

alex: I'll update here when the ROCm kernel PR lands and post microbench results. If anyone wants early access to the mi250 run ping me.

sam: Thanks — this will make kernel selection + sequence-length-aware paths explicit in the runtime which is what we've been missing. :rocket:
